questions.prompt: Which of these are perfect squares? Choose all that apply.
Which number can you tell is NOT a perfect square just from its last digit?
questions.explain: Squares never end in 2, 3, 7 or 8. The others are all squares: 36², 45², 81².
There are 15 odd numbers from 1 to 29, so the sum is 15² = 225.

questions.prompt: Work out 35² − 34² without finding either square.
How many non-square whole numbers lie between 12² and 13²?
questions.explain: Between n² and (n + 1)² there are 2n numbers: 2 × 12 = 24 (from 145 to 168).

questions.prompt: Explain why a perfect square can never end in 7.
questions.modelAnswer: The last digit of a square depends only on the last digit of the number being squared. Squaring 0–9 gives last digits 0, 1, 4, 9, 6, 5, 6, 9, 4, 1. None of these is 7, so no square can end in 7.
rubric: Last digit depends only on the last digit
questions.explain: Criterion C: a complete, logical argument.

questions.prompt: In the locker puzzle, locker 36 is toggled by everyone whose number is a factor of 36. What happens to it?
options: 9 people toggle it, so it ends up open
8 people toggle it, so it ends up closed
6 people toggle it, so it ends up closed
questions.explain: 36 has 9 factors (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36). An odd number of toggles leaves it open.
